obligations.note: The new route POST /payees/{id}/reopen uses the privileged action manage_payees with mfa=False, and the registered exhaustive control test test_privileged_routes_require_mfa fails on exactly this route. EXC-0180 covers only 'the reconciliation batch account', but the route serves any session holding manage_payees (for example payments_officer) with no account or network restriction in code.

EXC-0180 is approved by a risk_owner (Omar Haddad, not the requester), unexpired and scoped to MFA-1/payments.routes. However, the deviation as built is broader than its stated scope, and the recorded compensating control (internal network restriction) does not appear in the change. An out-of-scope exception doesn't count.

Ticket CHG-25044 is standard and was approved by change manager Erik Brandt on 2026-10-22, before review. Its components (payments.http, routes, service, store) cover app.py, routes.py, service.py and store.py.
Sofia Santos, a change_approver for payments and not the author (Jonah Weiss), gave a code_review approval on head 34162ea9.
The change has a single commit, and both approvals name that head commit.

The CI run on head has result 'failure' with 1 failing test, the registered MFA-1 control test. The JUnit report is also timestamped 2026-10-23 on a personal host (dev-laptop-7.local), before the commit was authored, so it is not credible evidence for this commit.
The change touches security-sensitive payments.routes, payments.http and payments.store. Ines Halvorsen (security_reviewer) gave a security_review approval on the head commit.
Ledger entry ACR-0404 (MFA-1 control test) covers routes.py, which this change alters in behaviour, so it has lapsed. No valid new evidence of the same strength exists; the rerun control test fails.

The new reopen_payee records an audit event with actor, action, target and time via _audit. However, the only control test is sample-coverage, and the CI report's provenance is unreliable for the head commit.

The new store.reopen_payee execute call uses a fixed literal with a bound parameter, which looks compliant. However, the exhaustive SQL control test result comes from a CI report that cannot be tied to the head commit.
store.py changed but no NPI columns are written by the new statement. The control test pass cannot be relied on because the JUnit report predates the commit and comes from a local machine.
app.py and service.py contain log call sites, though the new code adds none. The only evidence is a sample-coverage test in an untrustworthy CI report.

Reopening sets status to open and clears closed_at on any payee, which resets the retention clock and can reopen payees whose NPI was already purged. No guard exists and no retention test covers the new path.

summary: The change adds a privileged manage_payees route without MFA. The cited exception EXC-0180 is limited to the reconciliation batch account, while the code exposes the route to any manage_payees session and implements no compensating restriction. The change's own CI run failed on the MFA-1 control test, and its JUnit report predates the commit and comes from a personal machine, so CHG-4 is not met and the lapsed MFA-1 evidence has no replacement. Ticket, independent code review and security review are in order, but the MFA-1, EXC-1, CHG-4 and LAP-1 violations require rejection.
